Date: Tue, 6 May 2025 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Multiplexed sockets capacity check-in + proposed quota

Thanks for the call this morning, Logan — helpful session. A couple quick clarifications from our side so the engineering team can size the pilot: 

1) Concurrency model: our service opens a persistent upstream connection per application instance and then multiplexes requests over that socket. Typical instance fan-out is 6-10 workers, but we can scale to 25 in bursts.
2) Latency targets: 95th percentile < 300ms for prompt sizes under 512 tokens. For streaming responses we need a stable first-byte < 120ms.
3) Throughput: avg sustained tokens/sec per instance ~ 450 tokens/sec, peak bursts up to 2k tokens/sec for short windows (10-30s).

Can you confirm whether Redwood can support a soft cap per-connection concurrent request count (we'd ideally keep active parallel requests per socket <= 20), and a per-account burst allowance to handle traffic spikes? Also please send a suggested quota that we can review internally.

Attaching our current QA workload profile (small CSV).

Thanks,
Alex Dumas
Platform Engineering, FintechX

Subject: Re: Multiplexed sockets capacity check-in + proposed quota

Alex — great notes, thanks. Quick recap on what we heard and what we'll propose: 

- Internalized model of your traffic: persistent sockets per instance, ~6–10 concurrent workers, bursts to 25; average token rates and short bursts as you described.
- Redwood suggested baseline: per-account concurrent request soft cap = 2,000 parallel token-producing requests across the account, with per-socket recommendation of <= 16 active parallels to avoid head-of-line contention on our runtime.
- Burst allowance: additive short-burst pool of 5,000 parallel tokens (applied as token-equivalent credits over a 60s sliding window) to handle traffic spikes.

Open questions for sizing: 
- Do you expect sustained streaming sessions (open websocket-like streams) more than ~200 concurrent active streams during peak? That affects memory/KV cache sizing.
- Any single-request sequences that are routinely >1k tokens? Those impact per-token cost and may need a different model.

I attached a quick qualification matrix and a first-pass rate proposal. Ben — looping you for pricing confirm and whether we should propose canary ramp steps (50 -> 200 -> full pilot). Lauren — can you weigh in on SLO enforcement and monitoring hooks we’ll provide (traces, token-level breakdowns)?

Next step: Alex, can you confirm typical peak concurrent streams and any long-tail (>1k token) requests by EOD tomorrow? We'll revise quota to match.

Cheers,
Logan Wright
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Date: Wed, 7 May 2025 08:41:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Multiplexed sockets capacity check-in + proposed quota

Logan — thanks. Answers below: 

- Peak concurrent active streams across all instances: ~320 during trading windows, sustained for 2–3 minutes. We can throttle on our side but prefer platform-level burst handling to avoid dropped UX.
- Long requests: about 4% of requests exceed 1k tokens (batch summarization jobs). Those are less latency-sensitive but consume KV and memory on the server side.
- We can accept a per-socket guidance of <=16 active parallels; we’ll implement backpressure if you recommend lower.

Also, one commercial ask: FintechX will need a formal written quota/limit to include with procurement. Can you provide a one-page summary that includes soft caps, burst pool behavior, and an escalation path if we hit the cap in production?

Going to run this with procurement and SRE and circle back.

Best,
Alex

Alex — appreciate the fast follow. Drafting the one-page quota summary now; attaching a clean PDF for procurement that captures: soft caps (2,000 concurrent account-level parallels), per-socket recommended max (16), burst pool rules (5,000 tokens over 60s sliding window), and an escalation flow (support SLA, on-call, and escalation to capacity engineering).

Operational notes: if FintechX expects to flip to dedicated capacity later, we can convert the soft caps to committed throughput (reserved capacity) with predictable latency SLOs and a migration runbook. For the pilot, proposed ramp: 50 concurrent -> 250 -> 750 over three weeks with monitoring checkpoints and automated rollback to the last healthy level if error-rate or p95 latency breaches thresholds.

Can we lock the pilot start for May 19th? If so, I’ll send a formal quote and a DocuSign for the pilot terms.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Senior Sales, Redwood Inference
